subject: Post-demo: multi-workload benchmarking proposal & GPU comparison
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jason Smith <jason.smith@lumencloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: multi-workload benchmarking proposal & GPU comparison

Jason — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap from our demo and the proposed next steps to validate Dedicated capacity for LumenCloud's real-time search assistant workload.

Key takeaways from call:
- Target SLOs you reiterated: p95 token generation latency <= 120ms for short completion (<= 128 tokens), and streaming tail latency (first byte) <= 220ms for live user sessions.
- Typical request profile: 65% short completions (<=128 tokens), 25% mid (128–512), 10% long (>512/stream).
- Peak concurrency target: sustained 180 concurrent sessions during peak; expected average concurrency ~60.
- Business ask: estimate reserved throughput and GPU mix for a pilot (30k MAUs, growth 3–6 months), and a bench plan that exercises mixed workloads + streaming.

Proposed pilot validation (we discussed verbally; attached is the write-up):
1) Multi-workload bench: run three traffic profiles (short-only, mixed, streaming-heavy) against candidate GPU types (H100 80GB, A100 80GB, L4/Inferentia where applicable). We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, token throughput, and effective cost/TPS.
2) Reserved throughput sizing: we provide a per-GPU reserved throughput matrix (requests/sec and tokens/sec) plus a recommended safety buffer.
3) Streaming run: end-to-end streaming test with simulated user sessions (50k real-time connections at scale) to capture first-byte and chunk latencies and KV cache behavior.
4) Quality check: run your production prompt set (we'll use anonymized/hashed prompts) to ensure quantization/FP16 paths don't degrade output.

Next steps for this week:
- You: share a sanitized sample of typical prompts and the estimated token distribution (we only need distribution, not PII).
- Us: produce the bench plan and a short GPU comparison brief (attached) plus a baseline reserved-throughput calc.
- Schedule: propose a 90-minute pilot kickoff for next Tue or Wed; we need a point of contact from infra to open networking for the pilot env.

Attachments: multiworkload-bench-plan.md (bench steps and metrics), gpu-comparison-brief.pdf (tradeoffs and cost math), reserved-throughput-calc.xlsx (initial sizing).

Thanks — I copied Karthik and Ben to surface the sizing assumptions and the ops checklist.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Jason Smith <jason.smith@lumencloud.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Anu Rao <anu@lumencloud.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 10:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: multi-workload benchmarking proposal & GPU comparison

Vanessa — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. We reviewed the high-level ask internally; a few clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) Latency targets — p95 120ms for short completions is our goal, but realistically we can tolerate up to 160ms for p95 during spikes if throughput is preserved. Streaming first-byte <= 220ms is a hard requirement for user experience.
2) Concurrency — 180 concurrent sessions at peak is rough; that includes both active token-generation and idle streaming connections (we estimate ~25% of those will be idle but still holding a socket). Please include idle-connection overhead in the reserved capacity math.
3) Data/QA — we can provide a sanitized prompt distribution and a 1-hour trace sample from last week's traffic. We'll need a narrow NDA addendum for the trace sample; I can loop in legal if needed.

For GPUs: our infra prefers NVIDIA H100 where possible but cost is a concern; we'd like A100 comparison (perf + cost) and a small-run on L4 for short-completion optimization if Redwood supports it.

If you can share an estimated calendar for the pilot (start window and duration), I can confirm infra availability next Tue/Wed.

Thanks,
Jason
Director of Engineering, LumenCloud
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jason Smith <jason.smith@lumencloud.com>, Anu Rao <anu@lumencloud.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: multi-workload benchmarking proposal & GPU comparison

Adding my sizing notes inline and a tuned proposal so we can converge quickly.

Quick assumptions (please confirm):
- Model family: medium-sized decoder transformer (approx 13B param) for mixed workloads; we'll include a 70B variant for cost/latency contrast if you want to test.
- Avg token length: short=60 tokens, mid=220, long=950.
- Token generation cost baseline: H100 ~ 1.0x perf baseline; A100 ~ 0.85x vs H100 for FP16 workloads we use; L4 optimized for short completion can be ~1.2x cost-efficient for short profiles but limited memory for long requests.
- KV-cache: for streaming chat we need to measure effective cache hit-rate — if your sessions commonly do context reuse, effective throughput per GPU increases materially.

Pilot sizing proposal (30-day pilot capacity target; assumes 2-week active bench window):
- Option A (H100-primary): reserve 6 x H100 80GB nodes -> sustained reserved throughput ~ 1,200 short-completions/sec (with 1.25x buffer), supports 180 peak concurrent interactive sessions with streaming, and gives headroom for long-run batching. Estimated monthly pilot cost: (placeholder) — we'll provide exact numbers in the calc sheet.
- Option B (A100 mixed): reserve 8 x A100 80GB nodes -> similar throughput but higher token latency for some long requests; cheaper per-node. Good compromise if budget-constrained.
- Option C (L4 optimized for short-heavy): reserve 10 x L4 inference nodes -> best cost for short-only traffic, but streaming long sessions and KV-heavy chat will suffer due to memory limits.

Operational notes:
- We'll run a bench that ramps to 120% of your projected peak for each profile and capture CPU/GPU utilization, network stalls, and p99 tail latencies.
- Need an infra contact to provide a small test VPC/peering or staging creds.
- We'll instrument with per-request tracing so we can correlate latency spikes to cache misses or batch boundaries.

If these options look reasonable I can turn the calc into concrete cost numbers and an ops playbook. Vanessa — do you want me to own the pilot-runbook doc and coordinate with Ben on the benchmark harness?

—
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

From: Jason Smith <jason.smith@lumencloud.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: multi-workload benchmarking proposal & GPU comparison

Karthik/Vanessa — this is helpful, thanks. We prefer Option A if the cost delta vs Option B is within ~15% given our latency sensitivity.

Action items I can own this week:
- Get the sanitized prompt distribution and a 1-hour trace sample to Vanessa (I'll get legal on the quick NDA addendum for the trace).
- Provide a staging VPC + one infra contact (Anu) for network setup.
- Confirm pilot kickoff: tentatively Tue 20 Jun 2028 10:00 PT — I should have final confirmation by Mon EOD.

Vanessa/Karthik/Ben — please share the finalized bench plan and the reserved-throughput calc by Monday so we can review before kickoff.

Appreciate it — looking forward to the pilot.
